ca_drifter_smoking_boulder.blurb: A big, well-known block on the Buttermilks Main hillside outside Bishop, in the Eastern Sierra, sitting up the slope beyond the Peabody Boulders. All 11 problems are boulder problems, and the best ones are concentrated on the north face. The grades run from a single easy V0 warm-up through a solid middle of V4 to V6, with a few harder lines above that and one problem at V11. Expect sandy, flat landings and an old-school feel; the headline line here is a long-standing V7 that draws plenty of attention. It is a short uphill walk from the road, and it suits strong intermediates and up far better than beginners.

ca_mermaids_the.blurb: A small cluster of granite-style river boulders just downstream of the Cosumnes River Gorge near Placerville, in the Sierra foothills. Eleven boulder problems range from V3 up to a V7, with most landing around V3 and V4, so it fits intermediate climbers best. Problems are short, often a move or two, and many landings are bare rock, so bring several pads and a spotter. The slabs on the walk in turn very slick when wet, and warm months bring rattlesnakes, ticks and poison oak. Cooler months are the more comfortable time to visit.

ca_jbmf_boulder.blurb: The busiest block in the JBMF group of boulders in Joshua Tree National Park, on the northern edge of the roadside rocks near Intersection Rock. It holds 11 problems, most of them easy to moderate, from VB up to V3, with four at V3 and two V5 problems at the top, including the area's best-known face line. The rock is textured desert stone with good friction, so footwork and balance pay off. The block stands roughly 15 to 20 feet tall, the north side is steep and the west side is closer to vertical. Shade is scarce, so early or late sessions are more pleasant.

ca_lower_kern_river_canyon_bouldering.blurb: Boulders scattered through the lower Kern River canyon along Highway 178, east of Bakersfield on the way up toward Lake Isabella. Stones sit in the riverbed and on the banks, and most are close to the road. Nine problems run from V2 to V8, mostly in the V5 to V7 range, plus two short roped lines around 5.10. Summer flows can polish and flood some lines, and the river itself deserves caution when high. Winter is the usual choice, and several areas lie across the water, which is easiest to cross when flows are low. Expect a quiet canyon.

ca_hatrack_the.blurb: A low, elongated boulder in Joshua Tree National Park, set right beside the paved lot at Cap Rock. Its 11 problems are friction and slab climbs, almost all very easy: roughly eight sit at VB or V0, a couple at V1 and a lone V3. The walk is virtually nothing, which makes it a convenient warm-up or an outing for beginners and kids learning footwork. Balance and precise feet matter more than strength. Bring a couple of pads for the slabs, and plan for early or late hours in warm weather since the desert sun is strong.
ca_hatrack_the.parking_note: Use the paved lot on the south end of the Cap Rock loop; the boulder sits just behind the accessible parking spaces.
ca_hatrack_the.approach: Essentially none: the boulder is a few steps from the paved lot, along the Cap Rock nature trail.
